sections.content: How many people are "print finishing and binding workers"?

9,030 people

were counted on the census as "print finishing and binding workers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Print finishing and binding workers bind books and other publications and finish printed items by hand or machine.

People who had this job were generally older

The occupation of "print finishing and binding workers" had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "print finishing and binding workers", 15.1% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "print finishing and binding workers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "print finishing and binding workers" included:

  • hire services managers and proprietors
  • local government administrative occupations
  • electrical service and maintenance mechanics and repairers

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "print finishing and binding workers" there were more men than women (69.4% compared with 30.6%).

This means "print finishing and binding workers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "textiles, printing and other skilled trades".

Men made up 69.4% and women made up 30.6% of "print finishing and binding workers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "print finishing and binding workers" included:

  • fishing and other elementary agriculture occupations (other)
  • health and safety managers and officers
  • architects

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "print finishing and binding workers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged between 30 and 49 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "print finishing and binding workers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "print finishing and binding workers", 8.9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had an older age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (81.1% compared with 18.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (90.2%) than self-employed (9.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Leeds, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
